```{r, include = FALSE}
# Generating the necessary libraries for this project
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyverse)
library(purrr)
library(gt)
library(flextable)
library(lintr)

# Define a function to read, clean,
# and summarize one year of air quality data

#Ozone is assumed to be in ppm unless ozone_units = "ppb" is specified.
clean_air_quality <- function(file_path, ozone_units = c("ppm", "ppb")) {

  ozone_units <- match.arg(ozone_units)
  pollutants <- c("CO", "PM25", "O3")

  # Function that read the CSV file,
  # renaming the required columns
  air_data <- readr::read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    # Renaming pollutant columns and formatting data
    dplyr::rename(
      dplyr::all_of(c(
        date = "Date",
        CO = "Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration",
        PM25 = "Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration",
        O3 = "Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration"
      ))
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      date = lubridate::mdy(date)
    )

  # Converting O3 from ppm to ppb when requested
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    air_data <- air_data |>
      dplyr::mutate(O3 = .data$O3 * 1000)
  }

  # Grouping records by date and calculate the daily
  #mean for each pollutant along with detecting duplicates
  air_data <- air_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$date) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(pollutants),
        \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::distinct()

  # Replacing negative pollutant values with zero
  pollutants <- c("CO", "PM25", "O3")

  for (pollutant in pollutants) {
    air_data[[pollutant]][
      !is.na(air_data[[pollutant]]) &
        air_data[[pollutant]] < 0
    ] <- 0
  }

  air_data
}

# Reading and cleaning the data for each year
aq2018 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2018.csv")
aq2019 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2019.csv")
aq2020 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2020.csv")

## Combining the yearly datasets into one data frame
dataset_final <- dplyr:: bind_rows(
  aq2018,
  aq2019,
  aq2020
)

#Preview the combined data and review summary statistics
head(dataset_final)
summary(dataset_final)
```
## Function:

### Does the order change your results?
- **ANSWER:** Yes, the order changes my results. It is important to clean the data such as excluding incorrect results, duplicated results, incorrect units to their proper units before undergoing any potential calculations such as the proper conversions, re-evaluating negative values, etc. and finally combining the datasets into the respective categories to establish the proper data. 

## Table:
```{r, include = FALSE}
# Function: Calculate minimum and maximum pollutant concentrations for one year.
# Arguments:
#   data: Air quality data frame containing CO, PM25, and O3 columns.
#   year: Year represented by the data.
# Returns:
#   A one-row data frame containing the year and minimum and maximum
#   concentrations for each pollutant.

pollutant_summary <- function(data, year) {
  #calculating our minimum and maximum for the following pollutants:
  data |>
    summarise(
      co_min = min(.data$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      co_max = max(.data$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      pm25_min = min(.data$PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      pm25_max = max(.data$PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      o3_min = min(.data$O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      o3_max = max(.data$O3, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Calculate the summaries for each year and combine them into one data frame.
all_summaries <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pollutant_summary(aq2018, 2018) |> dplyr::mutate(Year = 2018),
  pollutant_summary(aq2019, 2019) |> dplyr::mutate(Year = 2019),
  pollutant_summary(aq2020, 2020) |> dplyr::mutate(Year = 2020)
) |>
  dplyr::select(Year, dplyr::everything())

all_summaries <- all_summaries |>
  dplyr::mutate(Year = as.character(Year))

# Creating a formatted table with readable column
#headings with pollutant results rounded to
#3 decimal places
ft <- flextable::flextable(all_summaries) |>
  flextable::set_header_labels(
    Year = "Year",
    co_min = "CO Minimum",
    co_max = "CO Maximum",
    pm25_min = "PM2.5 Minimum",
    pm25_max = "PM2.5 Maximum",
    o3_min = "O₃ Minimum",
    o3_max = "O₃ Maximum"
  ) |>
  flextable::colformat_num(j = 2:7, digits = 3) |>
  flextable::width(j = 1, width = 0.8) |>
  flextable::autofit()
# Formatting our table with centered header text
#and caption
ft <- ft |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = "Minimum and Maximum Concentrations 
    of CO, O₃, and PM2.5 for Years: 2018, 2019, 2020"
  ) |>
  flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header")
# Adding horizontal between rows and vertical lines between columns
ft <- ft |>
  flextable::hline(
    border = officer::fp_border(color = "gray60", width = 0.5),
    part = "body"
  ) |>
  flextable::vline(
    border = officer::fp_border(color = "gray60", width = 0.5),
    part = "all"
  )

# Output: table
ft
```

## Plots
### Plot 1: CO and O3 by month.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Summarize monthly means, standard deviations, sample sizes, and
# approximate 95% confidence interval margins for CO and O3.
plot1 <- function(data) {
  monthly_avg <- data |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$months) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_CO = mean(.data$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_CO = sd(.data$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_CO = sum(!is.na(.data$CO)),
      CI_CO = 1.96 * sd(.data$CO, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.data$n_CO))),

      mean_O3 = mean(.data$O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_O3 = sd(.data$O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_O3 = sum(!is.na(.data$O3)),
      CI_O3 = 1.96 * sd(.data$O3, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.data$n_O3))),

      .groups = "drop"
    )

  monthly_avg
}

# Add month and year values derived from each observation's date.
dataset_final <- dataset_final |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    months = lubridate::month(date)
  )

# Calculate the monthly CO and O3 summaries.
monthly_avg <- plot1(dataset_final)

# Reshape the summaries into a format suitable for plotting both pollutants.
monthly_long <- monthly_avg |>
  select(months, mean_CO, CI_CO, mean_O3, CI_O3) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -months,
    names_to = c(".value", "pollutant"),
    names_pattern = "(mean|CI)_(CO|O3)"
  )
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Plot monthly means and their approximate 95% confidence intervals.
# Separate facets give CO and O3 their own y-axis scales.
ggplot(monthly_long,
       aes(x = months, y = mean, color = pollutant)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - CI, ymax = mean + CI),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~pollutant, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average of CO and O3 Concentrations",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Average Concentration",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

**NOTE**:

- CO is shown above O₃ because its average concentration is higher. The separate ranges make the monthly point estimates and their respective 95% confidence intervals easier to read.

### Plot 2: PM2.5 by month and year. 
```{r, echo = FALSE}

#Extracting month from the dataset
dataset_final <- dataset_final |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    months = lubridate::month(date),
    year = lubridate::year(date)
  )

# Calculate the average PM2.5 concentration for each year and month.
plot2 <- function(data) {

  monthly_pm25 <- data |>
    group_by(year, months) |>
    summarise(
      mean_PM25 = mean(.data$PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  monthly_pm25
}

# Run function to create the montly PM2.5 summary data
monthlypm25 <- plot2(dataset_final)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Plot monthly PM2.5 averages, using a separate line for each year.
ggplot(monthlypm25,
       aes(x = months, y = mean_PM25,
           color = factor(year), group = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Average PM2.5 Concentration",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

## Interpretation:
In 2-3 sentences, describe the patterns you see in your tables and plots. For example: Do any pollutants show seasonal patterns? Do any years stand out? Keep in mind which months have less data.

- **ANSWER:** The plots suggest that CO and O₃ often move in opposite directions, with peaks in one tending to coincide with lower concentrations in the other. PM2.5 fluctuates across months and years rather than showing a consistent trend; interpret apparent seasonal patterns cautiously because some months have fewer observations (after April of 2020 due to COVID-19).
